simple: Lots of Roblox players use a mouse and keyboard, so your game should work well with them. This page shows how to detect key presses and mouse clicks with `UserInputService`, and how to change, hide, or lock the mouse pointer. For most game actions, Roblox suggests the Input Action System, but `UserInputService` is great for general key and mouse input.
analogy: `UserInputService` is like a doorbell camera for your keyboard and mouse. Every time a key is pressed or released, it rings and tells your script which one.
keyPoints: The Input Action System is the simplest way to support many devices for actions like jump or sprint.
`UserInputService.InputBegan` fires when a key or mouse button is pressed, and `InputEnded` fires when it is released.
The second value these events give you, often called `processedEvent` or `gameProcessed`, is `true` if something else already used that input, like typing in chat.
`UserInputService:IsKeyDown()` checks if a key is held right now.
Lock the pointer with `MouseBehavior` set to `LockCenter` or `LockCurrentPosition`, and unlock with `Default`. `InputChanged` still reports how far the mouse moved.

terms.UserInputService: The service that tells LocalScripts about keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad input.
terms.InputObject: The info about one input, such as `KeyCode` (which key) and `Position` (where the mouse was).
terms.KeyCode: The name of a key or button, like `Enum.KeyCode.E` or `Enum.KeyCode.Space`.
terms.processed event: An input that the game already used for something else, like typing in a TextBox. Usually you ignore it.
terms.mouse icon: The little pointer picture that moves with the mouse.
terms.delta: How much something changed. A mouse delta of `(5, -2)` means it moved 5 pixels right and 2 pixels up since the last check.
terms.LockCenter: Keeps the mouse pointer stuck in the middle of the screen, common in first-person shooters.

example.title: Press E to say hello
example.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	-- Ignore keys used for other things, like typing in chat
	if gameProcessed then
		return
	end

	if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E then
		print("Hello! You pressed E")
	elseif input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
		print("You clicked at", input.Position)
	end
end)
explain: `InputBegan` runs every time the player presses a key or mouse button.
If `gameProcessed` is true, the player was probably typing in chat, so we stop.
If the key was E, we print a hello message.
If it was a left mouse click (`MouseButton1`), we print where on the screen they clicked.

watchOut: Forgetting to check `gameProcessed`. Your E action will fire while players type the letter E in chat.
Using `UserInputService` in a server Script. It only works in LocalScripts.
Locking or hiding the mouse and never giving it back. Players will not be able to click menus.
Only supporting the keyboard. Mobile and console players need other ways to do the same action.
